paper.title: Measuring the Welfare Effects of Shame and Pride

claims.claim: YMCA balance descriptives and two-sided balance-test p values.
The effects of public recognition on YMCA attendance.
OLS and Tobit estimates of WTP by YMCA attendance, including curvature statistics.
WTP models restricted to attendance intervals near expected attendance.
Effects of public recognition and financial incentives on charitable-effort points.
WTP models by effort level in the charitable-contribution experiments.
Structural parameter estimates and financial-incentive consistency checks.
Welfare estimates of public recognition in the charitable experiments.
Welfare estimates under scale-up scenarios for the YMCA.
Additional numerical results reported in the abstract and main text.

findings.description: The master script requires a user-specific Windows root and expects folder names that differ in case from the supplied package. The Prolific build also contains a standalone debugger break. The R translation used the supplied package path, created expected output folders, normalized the survey_id merge key, and removed the debugger break.
findings.evidence: master_file.do defines rootdir only for username billy; it sets Raw data while the supplied directory is Raw Data. Prolific_Build.do has `break` immediately after import.
findings.suggested_fix: Define rootdir portably, use the supplied folder casing, create required output directories, and remove the debugger break.

findings.description: Gen_Vars.do initializes and later reads switch_preference but increments switch. The translated build increments the initialized variable to preserve the apparent intended switch count.
findings.evidence: The loop increments `switch`; consistency indicators use `switch_preference`.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the increment target to switch_preference in the shipped build script.

findings.description: Several structural estimates and scale-up welfare values differ from the published precision after direct translation; the disagreement is computational and is not a judgment on the scientific conclusion.
findings.evidence: Tables 7 and 9 contain translated values and percentile intervals in results; see the individual discrepancies and notes.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare Stata's Tobit and clustered bootstrap implementation, including its exact finite-sample and random-number behavior, with the R translation.

limitations: Stata was unavailable, so all reported computations are from a direct R translation. The R and Stata random number generators differ, including for the 1,000-replication cluster bootstrap.
The 1,000 bootstrap attempts yielded 999 valid YMCA, 1,000 valid Prolific, 1,000 valid Berkeley, and 994 valid BU replications because some structural roots were not real.
Figures are not separately itemized as claims; the abstract, data-derived main-text numerical results, and Tables 1-9 are checked here.
No robustness analysis or judgment about scientific correctness was performed.
